# Answers to the included review questions

Selected task: `6fde852adb54` / original `training:963c33f8`.
The answer is backed by a runnable task-local sampler, finite-rival lesson gate,
exact counterexample and live Racket evidence. The gate and sampler are
**proposed workspace tools**; production sampling and canonical authority are
unchanged by this work.

## Q1 — generator-shortcuts

### Strongest concrete rival tested

Keep the canonical independent falling-column mechanics, tip stopping,
near-floor trigger, tie breaks and shelf clearing. Change just the body-column
landing criterion: choose the obstacle-component column with the **longest
contiguous vertical run**, rather than the greatest **total number of obstacle
cells**. Prefer the nearest column, then the lower column index, as the
canonical rule does. This is a plausible visual interpretation of the current
notes' “tallest column.” It is stronger than always falling straight down:
it preserves the special landing behavior illustrated by the demonstrations.

This rival fits all three canonical demonstration outputs. It also fits the
official query and all eight public input geometries (four original scenes and
their reflections). These are executed comparisons, not inferred labels;
`checks/questions/probe.json` contains the source-bound Racket records and the
full witness. The implemented rival is in
`repo/generators/6fde852adb54/workspace/questions/question_gate.py`.

### Exact lawful disagreement

Use this 14×14 input. Coordinates below are zero-based. Colors are field 7,
body 9, tip 1 and obstacle 5.


The mover occupies columns 3–5. Columns 3 and 4 end in tips and fall to the
floor. The body-only source at column 5 encounters a single bottom component
with these per-column measurements:

| Component column | Obstacle rows | Total count | Longest contiguous run |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| 5 | 11, 12, 13 | 3 | 3 |
| 6 | 8, 10, 11, 13 | 4 | 2 |
| 7 | 8, 9, 10 | 3 | 3 |

The canonical rule chooses column 6 and paints body color 9 at rows 11–13.
The rival chooses column 5, which wins its nearest-column tie. There are
exactly six output disagreements:

| Row | Column | Canonical Racket | Rival |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 11 | 5 | 5 | 9 |
| 11 | 6 | 9 | 5 |
| 12 | 5 | 5 | 9 |
| 12 | 6 | 9 | 7 |
| 13 | 5 | 5 | 9 |
| 13 | 6 | 9 | 5 |

The ten-cell component is four-connected. Four isolated obstacles in column 0
supply the other components, making five components and fourteen obstacle
cells in total. The field is the unique modal color, the top mover has the
required shape, and both tips have space to fall. `self_check` returns an empty
error list. The full canonical and rival output grids are retained in
`checks/questions/probe.json`; the exact runnable input is also the query in
`checks/questions/ambiguous_lesson.json`.

### Racket verification and emitted support

The final bounded probe made 14 unique canonical Racket applications, including
all eight public geometries, one ordinary generated control, the witness and
four proposed sampler draws. Racket 8.10 matched the selected Python mirror on
every checked input. The default probe exited 0 in 3.854 seconds,
including the packet wrapper. `checks/questions/probe_run.json` records the
exact command, working directory, environment, source hashes and exit status.

**Current `generate()` does not emit a separating case for this rival.** This
conclusion has a structural basis: the public branch uses only the eight checked
geometries; role recoloring preserves the comparison. In the generalized
branch, distractors exclude the mover columns and cannot connect to previously
placed components. The active near-floor bar or L-shaped blob has contiguous
obstacle rows in every column; a tip stopper which joins the blob only extends
a contiguous column. Consequently total count and longest run coincide wherever
they decide a generated body landing. The one ordinary generated control is a
smoke check, not a statistical proof or broad census.

**The proposed `sample_witness` does emit such cases.** Every construction uses
the gapped component above, translated for the requested dimensions, optionally
reflected and role-recolored. Seed 17, sample indices 0–3 produced distinct
15×20, 23×14, 17×18 and 16×21 lawful inputs, each verified by Racket with six
rival disagreements. They are retained in `probe.json`. This is a small
witness sampler, not an implemented extension of production `generate()`.

## Q2 — qwen9-data-value

### One additional automated gate

Add a **query-aware gate for declared rival rules** when admitting self-contained
supervised episodes. For this task, test the longest-run rival above:

1. Validate the scene grammar and verify demonstration labels with the pinned
   canonical Racket program.
2. Check whether the rival predicts every demonstration output.
3. If it survives, independently execute the canonical rule on the query input
   and compare the rival's prediction. Reject or augment the demonstration set
   only if those query predictions differ.

The implemented `lesson_gate` reads no query answer. The reusable JSON CLI
accepts `{"demos": [...], "query": {"input": ...}}`, computes the query prediction
through Racket, and writes its report. Exit 0 means this finite gate passed;
exit 2 reports ambiguity, invalid data or reference failure. A pass does not
establish universal identifiability, source approval or training admission.

### Reproducible failure and useful positive controls

The three canonical demos plus the exact gapped-component query are valid,
correctly labelled examples, but the demos leave this two-rule distinction
unresolved. The gate reports `ambiguous`, with three matching demos and six
query differences. This is the reproducible teaching failure it catches.
`checks/questions/cli_ambiguous.json` records the expected CLI exit 2 and its
Racket-backed report.

Adding the exact witness as a labelled demonstration refutes the rival.
Four distinct proposed sampler queries then pass under the same four-demo
context; the query answers were never used as demonstrations. The standalone
`repaired_lesson.json` CLI check also exited 0. Conversely, the original
canonical query is answer-equivalent under both rules, so the unchanged three
demos correctly pass for that query (`cli_equivalent_report.json`). A gate
which rejected every surviving rival would incorrectly reject this control.

### False-positive boundary

A self-contained-episode policy may be too strict for intentional extrapolation
or a curriculum which explicitly supplies the rule or permits reliance on
previous episodes. In those settings, an episode can be useful even if these
demos alone do not separate the rival. Applying an overbroad or incorrectly
implemented rival outside its supported scene domain can also create a false
rejection. Restrict the gate to validated scenes and its stated training policy,
and preserve the answer-equivalent-query exception.

The current production support hole remains: because this rival agrees on
current generated queries, this query-aware gate alone will not create the
missing examples or reject those answer-equivalent episodes. Pair it with the
proposed witness sampler when testing or expanding this family, then require a
separating demo before querying the distinction. No production integration is
claimed here.

### Cheapest test and exact commands

The ten-test stdlib suite takes about 0.138 seconds in this checkout.
It covers the failed lesson, repaired lesson, equal-answer control, absent and
malicious query labels, invalid queries, incorrect demonstration labels,
reference failures, sampler boundaries, determinism and input purity. It uses
the Python mirror; the separate four-second bounded probe supplies live Racket
verification. There is no model job or large seed search.

From `WORK/`, after the packet's Racket setup:

```bash
PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 run_with_racket.py python3 \
  generators/6fde852adb54/workspace/questions/probe_questions.py \
  --out ../checks/questions/probe.json

PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 run_with_racket.py python3 \
  generators/6fde852adb54/workspace/questions/probe_questions.py \
  --lesson ../checks/questions/ambiguous_lesson.json \
  --out ../checks/questions/my_gate_report.json
```

The second command is expected to exit 2. Substitute `repaired_lesson.json` or
`answer_equivalent_lesson.json` for an expected exit 0. The workspace README
also gives the direct stdlib test command and API contract.

mechanics; no measured Qwen performance improvement is asserted.
